## Project Overview
Grounded review and UI/data work on TreeApp at `d:/5eliment/app/treeapp` (Five Elements). React Native / Expo field app: photograph trees, lock GPS, record measurements, sync to Supabase for the CARM admin panel. README still describes an early photo-and-form app; the code is a project-based survey, audit, task, and land-boundary system. Domain model is mainly `src/types/index.ts` plus Supabase migrations. Terminal is cmd.exe, not PowerShell. Python `-c` and pip do run. No successful Metro cache clear or Expo start is proven. No EAS build has produced or downloaded an APK. No local `:app:assembleRelease` has printed `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` / `BUILD FAILED`, an exit code paired with a Gradle log, or a package-task line. No markdown file has been read, and no `file_write_result` or diff has confirmed markdown contents. No script file under `scripts/` has been confirmed deleted. `.git/COMMIT_EDITMSG` was visible and open at 6:20:30 and has not been read; it is not an open tab from 9:22:25 through 9:48:12. Absence from the tab list is not deletion and not a read.

Latest environment is 10/5/2026, 9:48:12 PM (Asia/Calcutta, UTC+5:30). Context 135,898 tokens (68%), up from 134,213 (67%) at 9:38:04. It is not the 9:27 issued completion (Approved-tab / newer-task / audit / healthy-sick-dead claim still unreturned) and not the 9:35 completion (single-tree map and vibration). Confirmed no-diff path modifications, confirmed reads, SQL hit windows, two empty `tsc --noEmit` successes, the 6:35 APK directory listing, and the 11:29 deletion of `captureQueue.ts` only remain. The 9:24, 9:27, 9:29, 9:32, 9:35, and 9:38 issued searches, edits, and completions listed above are not completed work. The 9:38 write is a confirmed path modification of TreeMapScreen only, not a completed behavior change. The 9:48 batch adds no completed work.

## Key Technical Decisions
Proof rules that still bind: an interrupted `attempt_completion` is not a hunk and is not acceptance. The 10/5, 11:48:14, 12:06:23, 12:07:48, 12:14:38, and 12:20:55 `attempt_completion`s were each interrupted; each result text is intent only and each tool use is unsuccessful. The 9:24, 9:35, and 9:48 batches each add an `attempt_completion` whose result is only user feedback, each presented with an unnamed interruption notice. None is acceptance. Each feedback body is a distinct user request, not a source change, not a read, and not a deletion. The 9:27 `attempt_completion` was issued and has no tool result through 9:48:12, so it is not acceptance and not a successful completion. There is no successful `attempt_completion` from 12:09:16 through 9:48:12. A returned completion that only carries user feedback is not acceptance. An issued completion whose body is a claim about source behavior is not a read and not a write. A line citation inside an interrupted or unreturned completion is not a read. An issued tool call without a result is not a confirmed write, read, search, command, or todo change. An interrupted tool call confirms only that no result was returned. An interruption notice that names no tool and no path is not a write, not a hunk, and not a search result, and must not be assigned by name to the NotificationHistoryScreen edit, the TreeDetailScreen paddingBottom edit, the 9:24 or 9:25 HomeScreen searches, the 9:27 HomeScreen write, the 9:29 HistoryScreen edit, the 9:32 HomeScreen edit, the 9:35 search, the 9:38 TreeMapScreen write or edit, or the 9:48 ProfileScreen read. The 9:25 and 9:35 notices that the response was interrupted by a tool use result and that only one tool may be used at a time are that kind of notice; neither is a write. An IDE notice without a diff is not a hunk. A “Recently Modified Files” / “file was just edited” line is not a hunk, not a read, and not a `file_write_result`. A `file_write_result` that says `modified` but shows no diff confirms modification of that path only. A notice that changes were seen, or to treat them as the new baseline, does not supply a hunk and does not prove which bytes changed. A later such result for the same path does not show whether the bytes differ from an earlier one. The pre-9:20 TreeDetailScreen result, the pre-9:22 ProjectSelectScreen result, the 9:27 HomeScreen result, and the 9:38 TreeMapScreen result are each that kind of later no-diff modification. The 9:29, 9:32, 9:35, and 9:48 batches add no `file_write_result`. A no-diff write that precedes an issued edit of the same path is not that edit’s result. TypeScript problems printed inside a `file_write_result` confirm those quoted lines and that diagnostic only. Absence of compiler problems is not proof the file typechecks and not proof any symbol was removed. A later `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 with empty stdout confirms only that invocation’s reported success and no captured stdout. A prose claim that typecheck passed is not an invocation. A confirmed read of one slice does not prove text outside that slice. A later read or search supersedes earlier hits for those same printed lines only. A later no-diff write of the same path means earlier reads of that path are no longer proven current until a later result reprints lines. A search that returns after a no-diff write of the same path is current for the printed lines only as of that result; a `----` gap is not printed text. A later search does not erase an earlier confirmed read of lines it does not reprint. Search hits outside a later read are not reconfirmed, and their line numbers are unreliable if earlier lines in that file are now known to differ. A search-result header that does not restate the regex does not prove which pattern matched; when paired, the issued regex is the pattern. The 22-result, 5:43 1-result, 5:48 12-result, 5:54 6-result, 6:08 8-result, and 9:32 2-result headers are each not paired with an issued regex in the batch that returned them, so those patterns are unknown and must not be invented. The 9:32 result must not be assigned to the 9:24, 9:25, or 9:35 searches. The 6:04 “Found 0 results” header names no path, regex, or file pattern. The 6:08 “Found 8 results” header names no regex or file pattern and must not be assigned to any other search, including the 9:32 result and the 9:48 read. It is distinct from the earlier 11:35:49 “Found 8 results” printout and from the 9:32 “Found 2 results” printout. The 6:20 “Found 11 results” header is the return of the search issued at 6:15 (`INSERT INTO|tree_id|CREATE TRIGGER|tasks`, `*.sql` on `supabase`). Its groups are only `001_add_tree_columns.sql`. The 6:06 treeStore, 6:09 types, 6:11 TreeDetailScreen, 9:25 TaskScreen, and 9:29 HistoryScreen results are file reads (TreeDetailScreen as of that time only). The 9:27 HomeScreen and 9:38 TreeMapScreen results are no-diff writes, not reads. The 9:32 HomeScreen result is a search print of lines 84–86 and 88–90, not a write. The 9:35 and 9:48 batches have no file result. The 9:38 TreeMapScreen result is not the later issued edit. Printed search groups are hit context only. Zero groups means no file text. A command result that omits the command string does not by itself prove which command ran. Exit 0 with a listing or JSON confirms that printed listing or JSON only. Exit 1 whose stdout is a shell “not recognized” message confirms that failure text only. “Successfully deleted” one path confirms deletion of that path only. An `apply_patch` / `edit` / `write_to_file` body is intended text until a result says otherwise. When the result says `modified` with no diff, the path was modified and the body remains intended text, not a proven hunk and not a confirmed prior read. If the issued edit body is not in the batch that returns the no-diff result, do not invent the intended old or new text. The 9:29 HistoryScreen edit, the 9:32 HomeScreen edit, and the 9:38 TreeMapScreen edit have no result, so their old and new strings stay intended text except where the same characters were already printed. Assistant prose is intent only, including the 9:20 inset sentence, the 9:22 notifications sentence, the 9:24 dashboard sentence, the 9:27 Approved-tab sentence and completion claim, the 9:29 history-card sentence, the 9:35 map/vibration sentence, the 9:38 vibration-callback sentence, and the 9:48 profile-page sentence. An environment reminder list is not a build log and not an `update_todo_list` result. Reminder tables: 5:32:45 through 6:11:57 showed three planted-tree card items, all Completed; 6:15:09 showed item 1 In Progress and items 2 and 3 Pending; 6:20:30 showed items 1 and 2 In Progress and item 3 Pending. The 9:20:28 through 9:48:12 reminders instead say “You have not created a todo list yet.” All are reminder displays only, not an `update_todo_list` result, not a source change, and not acceptance. The 9:48 text is the later reminder display; it does not prove a todo write and does not erase that earlier displays showed those items. A visible-file, open-tab, or workspace-file line is not a read. An empty visible-files list and an empty open-tabs list are environment display only. A “You did not use a tool” error is automation, not a write. The 5:56 through 6:11 errors, two further ones by 6:20:30, and one each after the 9:20, 9:22, 9:24, 9:25, 9:27, 9:29, 9:32, 9:35, 9:38, and 9:48 batches are that automation. A tool-result error that a `search_files` was not executed because a tool was already used confirms only that the search did not run. A printed `ok` / `MISSING` line is that probe’s label, not a migration and not a full schema. A printed row count or delete JSON from an anon client confirms only what that invocation printed. A later sample-count JSON supersedes the live count for those named tables only as of that later invocation. A `select('*')` limited to 3 rows confirms the printed count, error field, and mapped sample fields only. Code that selects or writes a column is not proof the live column exists. A migration file’s printed SQL is file text of the printed lines only, not proof the migration ran. A TypeScript interface field is file text of the printed lines only. A user’s claim is not a deletion, not a new probe, and not an image read. An edit `old_string` is intended prior text, not a confirmed read, except where the same characters were already printed by a paired read or search. The TreeDetailScreen paddingBottom `old_string`, the NotificationHistoryScreen paddingBottom `old_string`, the 9:29 HistoryScreen allItems-merge `old_string`, the 9:32 HomeScreen filter/`taskMatchesTree` line, and the 9:38 TreeMapScreen dependency-array `old_string` were not previously printed. The 9:32 comment, signature, `const current = tasks`, `taskRank` sort, and return with `!isAuditTask(current)` were printed by the search and may be cited as those lines; the edit that would change them has no result. A select-count command is not a delete. A node script that `readFileSync`s `src/services/supabase.ts` and regex-extracts URL and anon key does not print that file. A content-wrapper attribute that claims a line range does not invent lines that are not printed. None of the items below is user-accepted.

Do not invent the pre-9:20 TreeDetailScreen hunk, the pre-9:22 ProjectSelectScreen hunk, the 9:27 HomeScreen hunk, the 9:29 HistoryScreen hunk, the 9:32 HomeScreen hunk, or the 9:38 TreeMapScreen hunk. Do not invent the 9:48 ProfileScreen body. Do not treat the TreeDetailScreen paddingBottom edit, the NotificationHistoryScreen edit, the 9:29 HistoryScreen edit, the 9:32 HomeScreen edit, or the 9:38 TreeMapScreen `focusTreeId` edit as landed. Do not invent `bottomPad`’s definition, `insets` math, or any inset padding. HistoryScreen line 96’s `useSafeAreaInsets()` is the only confirmed `insets` binding in that file, and only inside lines 80–189. Do not treat the 6:11 lines 250–319, the 2:25:58 lines 1057–1091, or the search windows 154–156 and 589–591 as current source after the pre-9:20 write. Do not assign that write to the Post-Audit edit or to the paddingBottom edit. Do not assign the ProjectSelectScreen write, the 9:27 HomeScreen write, the 9:29 HistoryScreen read, the 9:32 HomeScreen search, the 9:35 batch, the 9:38 TreeMapScreen write, or the 9:48 batch to either unreturned padding edit. Do not invent a taskService.ts search result or file body. Do not invent the regex of the 22-result, 5:43, 5:48, 5:54, 6:04, 6:08, or 9:32 searches. The 9:24, 9:25, and 9:35 regexes are known from the issued calls only; do not invent their hits and do not treat them as the same search, as the 9:27 write, as the 9:29 read, as the 9:32 result, as the 9:38 write, or as the 9:48 read. Do not treat the 9:48 user sentence as proof that ProfileScreen was modified or that it shows every project. Do not invent which file is “the all project page.” ProjectSelectScreen’s pre-9:22 no-diff write is a path modification only and is not that identification.

## Relevant Files & Code
- `src/screens/Profile/ProfileScreen.tsx`: no confirmed read. Was an open tab at 9:38:04; not listed as visible or as a tab at 9:48:12 (absence is not deletion). A `read_file` offset 1 limit 220 was issued at 9:48 and has no result. Do not invent lines 1–220.
- `src/screens/Home/HomeScreen.tsx`: 9:27 no-diff write (hunk unknown).
